title: HandoverLab: system-level handover simulator for 5G-Advanced and beyond-5G research
description: HandoverLab is an open-source, system-level simulator of 3GPP mobility procedures (baseline handover with Event A3, Release-16 conditional and DAPS handover, Release-18 L1/L2-triggered mobility, conditional handover with the location events of Release 18, dual connectivity) for many users in dense 5G-Advanced and beyond-5G networks, on a street grid, in an open area, along a highway or a high-speed railway, in an indoor office, in suburban and rural macro cells or under the earth-moving beams of a LEO satellite. It provides a TR 38.901 received-power radio model (TR 38.811 for the satellite) with optional TDL fast fading, SSB and UE receive beams and several carriers, an optional slot scheduler with MCS, TBS and HARQ and user-plane buffers at handover, an L3-filtered measurement chain, a radio-link failure model, an outcome label for every handover attempt, a plug-in interface for handover rules (including a measurement-prediction rule after TR 38.744), equal-budget tuning studies with paired statistics, and verification against hand-computed values, golden event-log fingerprints, the 3GPP large-scale calibration and ns-3 / 5G-LENA.
